clue.text: Only a fight — very nearly

parts.note: only, as in 'only just', means just
a bout is a boxing match or round of fighting

explanation.surface: Someone describes a contest that was the only one, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal synonym for almost or approximately.

clue.text: 24 during the month to have soup

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other, so the month's letters go round

parts.note: June is a month of the year
the answer to 24 across is an entitlement; a lien is a legal right to hold another's property

explanation.surface: Someone is told to eat soup at some point in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is a cross-reference: it stands for the answer to 24 across, an entitlement, which must then be swapped for a legal synonym before going inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Julienne is a clear broth containing thin strips of vegetables, a kind of soup.

clue.text: Quieter part of a car?

definitions.meaning: a thing that makes something quieter, a noise suppressor, as on a gun
the exhaust box of a vehicle, called a muffler in American English

explanation.surface: A question about which bit of a car is the most peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quieter' looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, a thing that makes quiet. In British English this exhaust box is what Americans call the muffler.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler fitted to an exhaust pipe reduces the noise of a vehicle's engine.

clue.text: Brave secretary in smart surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for smart is placed around the secretary's letters

parts.note: to smart is to sting or hurt, to ache
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A courageous secretary is found in fashionable surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun here, a Native American warrior, and 'smart' is the verb to hurt, not the adjective stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Apache are a Native American people.

clue.text: Cunning, but not to start with, having information on gas

indicators.note: not to start with means the opening letter of the word for cunning is dropped

parts.note: foxy means cunning or sly
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A sly person, at first lacking, gets the facts about a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is a gaseous chemical element, so it is an example of a gas.

clue.text: Do some work in the pool with dramatis personae given the same kind of role

definitions.text: given the same kind of role

parts.words: Do some work in the pool
parts.note: a typing pool is an office of typists, so working there means to type
the dramatis personae are the characters of a play, its cast

explanation.surface: An actor seems to be doing swimming-pool work alongside a play's characters, always in similar parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pool' suggests swimming, but it is a typing pool, a room of office typists.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor typecast is repeatedly assigned similar parts in plays or films.

clue.text: It is stupid to give credit to the fool

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: It is foolish to believe what a fool says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give credit to' sounds like trusting the fool; it only means the abbreviation stands before the word for fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly lacking in sense or sensitivity, dense.

clue.text: First class, (religious instruction), quite perplexed by review

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word class is taken

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

indicators.note: perplexed means the letters of quite are muddled up

explanation.surface: A top-class religious lesson leaves someone baffled by a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' looks like a phrase meaning excellent; only the first letter of 'class' is wanted. 'perplexed' turns QUITE into TIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A critique is a critical assessment of a work, the same as a critical write-up.

clue.text: From Alaska, ringing soldier in east Africa

indicators.note: from means the answer is drawn out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A soldier in East Africa telephones from Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was a local soldier or policeman serving colonial powers in East Africa.

clue.text: Plan the man took into south Carolina and Maine

indicators.note: took into means the man is received inside the letters for the two states

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man plans a trip into two American states.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan or arrangement.

clue.text: Slumber number

parts.note: a number here is a song, and one for slumber is sung to send a child to sleep

explanation.surface: A rhyming phrase for a sleepy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but a song or piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to make a baby fall asleep.

clue.text: Hamlet's dog?

parts.note: Hamlet is a prince of Denmark, a ... in rank, so his hound would be a large breed named for that nation

explanation.surface: A question about the pet of Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so he was literally a great Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Dane is a very large breed of dog, punningly suited to Denmark's famous prince.

clue.text: Uncle on manoeuvres found something elementary

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An uncle on army manoeuvres discovers something basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' means simple on the surface but points to particle physics. 'manoeuvres' rearranges UNCLEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, a fundamental particle of an atomic nucleus, hence elementary.

clue.text: Get bill some paper

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: An instruction to obtain a bill and a few sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets; 'bill' is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or come to possess it.

clue.text: Of great importance like a strong tremor?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a powerful quake could break the ground apart

explanation.surface: Something hugely significant is compared to a powerful earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a figurative synonym for momentous, and literally describes a quake that shakes the planet to pieces.

clue.text: Eccentric lady first had the fruit

indicators.note: first means the lady's name is placed ahead of the word for eccentric

parts.note: Hazel is a woman's name
a nut is an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: An odd woman got the fruit before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like it describes the lady, but it is the noun NUT, which comes after her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut is the edible nut of the hazel tree, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Gathering of birds only?

parts.note: birds is British slang for young women, and hen means female, so this is a women-only celebration rather than a flock

explanation.surface: A question about a flock made up purely of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'birds' are young women; this is the celebration held for a bride before her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a women-only celebration before a wedding, the British counterpart of a bachelorette party.

clue.text: Tell one's friend

definitions.meaning: to hint or make known, as a verb
a close companion, as a noun

explanation.surface: An instruction to inform one's pal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: the verb ends '-mate', the noun '-mit'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest or let it be known; an intimate is a very close confidant.

clue.text: Ignore stumbling military officer initially giving this shout

indicators.note: stumbling means the letters of ignore are tumbled into a new order
initially means only the first letters of military and officer are used

explanation.surface: A military officer trips and, disregarding it, gives a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroopers famously yell this cry when jumping from a plane, so it is a battle shout.

clue.text: Study made by single Buddhist resident

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
I is the Roman numeral for one, single
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Buddhist living locally makes a single study.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is an inhabitant or occupant of a place.

clue.text: Pudding about to be brought up to useless old fellow

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word for about is reversed, reading upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Pudding is brought back up by a feeble old man.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a traditional British steamed pudding; RE (about) reversed gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent or bumbling person, typically an old one.

clue.text: Not making much progress prying

definitions.meaning: poking one's nose into others' affairs

explanation.surface: Someone getting nowhere by being nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing describes inching slowly forward, and also being nosy or inquisitive.

clue.text: Old weaver can be found in the dictionary

definitions.meaning: an archaic term for someone who weaves
a famous American dictionary named after Noah ...

explanation.surface: An old weaver can be looked up in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Webster is an archaic word for a weaver and the name of a well-known American lexicon.

clue.text: Miscreant from western region to make an impression

parts.note: to etch is to engrave, making an impression on a surface

explanation.surface: A villain from the West tries to make his mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a despicable or wicked person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Ron leaves lounge-bar drunk to find source of caviare

indicators.note: drunk means the remaining letters of lounge-bar are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ron leaves the bar drunk to find caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' signals that the letters RON come out of LOUNGEBAR; 'drunk' rearranges the remaining LUGEBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large sturgeon whose roe is prized as caviar.

clue.text: Firing fuels laid out

indicators.note: out means the letters of fuels laid are rearranged, laid out differently

explanation.surface: Fuel stores are set out for firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a burst of simultaneous gunfire.

clue.text: Wave, I must travel round north America

indicators.note: round means the anagram of I must goes around north and America
travel means the letters of I must move into a new order

explanation.surface: A wave tells someone they must travel around North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel' rearranges I MUST to TSUMI, which goes round NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake.

clue.text: Not left an entitlement

definitions.meaning: the opposite of left, as a direction

explanation.surface: An entitlement that is not on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the opposite direction to left, and also a legal or moral claim.

clue.text: You started hoo-ha with Eve rewriting chant

indicators.note: started means only the first letter of you is taken
rewriting means the letters of hoo-ha and Eve are written again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone started a fuss with Eve by redrafting a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' turns HOOHA plus EVE into OHEAVEHO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional sailors' work cry sung while hauling ropes.
